# API coverage

Google Cloud coverage shows exactly what the shipped commands can do: which official Google services and operations have explicit generated commands, which safety class they use, and which official source backs each row. If an endpoint or workflow is not listed here, do not assume the skill supports it.

This is source coverage, not live account proof. It shows which official Google Cloud operations the tool generated commands for, how those operations are classified for safety, and which official source was used.

A good first coverage check is: search for the service and operation you plan to use, then confirm the row has the expected HTTP method, safety class, and source evidence before asking for a live read or plan.

Generated from the official Discovery directory on 2026-06-25T02:23:52Z UTC.

## How to read this ledger

The table is large because the tool exposes explicit named commands instead of one generic caller. Each included Google Cloud operation has a row with the generated command name, HTTP method, safety class, risk labels, and the source evidence used to create it.

Included services are Google Cloud Platform resource and admin APIs selected from the official Discovery directory. The tool also forces in a small set of core Cloud services from Google developer docs when they matter for normal GCP work: billing budgets, Cloud Asset, Cloud Billing, Compute Engine, GKE, Cloud DNS, Cloud Logging, Pub/Sub, Cloud SQL Admin, and Cloud Storage.

Excluded services are listed near the bottom. They are either non-preferred API versions or separate Google product families that should stay in their own tools, such as Google Ads, Google Analytics, Business Profile, Merchant, Search Console, Tag Manager, Workspace user APIs, Maps or consumer-content APIs, and YouTube.

Fallback sources are official Google sources used only when the selected Discovery document is missing or incomplete. In this ledger, Data Labeling uses an official `googleapis` proto fallback, and Application Integration v1 and v2 use Google's official REST reference because the live Discovery URL returns 404. Cloud Tasks and Analytics Hub are included from Discovery.

`0 unresolved Discovery gaps` means every selected source gap was either resolved through an official fallback or left out for a documented boundary reason. It does not mean a live Google Cloud account has been verified. Live account behavior still needs a separate safe-target run with real Application Default Credentials.

## Summary

The short summary below is the first check. The full table after it is the command lookup ledger.

## Boundary

- Source directory: `https://discovery.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis`
- Cloud docs hosts: cloud.google.com, docs.cloud.google.com
- Explicit core developer-doc services: billingbudgets, cloudasset, cloudbilling, compute, container, dns, logging, pubsub, sqladmin, storage
- Included only preferred entries from the official Discovery directory.
- Used official Google fallback sources only when a selected Discovery document was missing or unavailable.
- Excluded separate Google product families listed in the boundary data.
- No raw-request bridge or arbitrary URL bridge is part of this slice.
